doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Live radio music and listening to Coon-Sanders
summary: Gallodoro recalls networks with live bands and dinner music; Willcox recalls tuning in distant stations like Coon-Sanders from Bill Rank's room.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Radio was really important at this time, right? That’s how most people—
They had live music. Live music. At 6:00 you played dinner music you know, with a string orchestra and flute and clarinet and bassoon.

Well you see in 1925 with the Goldkette band sometimes I’d go down to Bill Rank’s room and it would be about 1:30 or 2:00 and he’d have the things on there and you’d hear eeeeee, and we were listening to Carleton Coon, Coon Sanders.
Yeah, Coon Sanders. Very popular. The Black Hawk, Chicago?
